title: Russia Hits Kyiv With 198-Weapon Mass Barrage as Three-Day Capitals Truce Expires
detail: Russia launched its largest strike on Kyiv in weeks in the early hours of September 8, ending the three-day pause on capital strikes that had coincided with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner's shuttle diplomacy between Moscow and Kyiv. The Ukrainian Air Force said it downed 142 of 166 drones and 31 of 32 cruise missiles, but 2 ballistic missiles got through along with an unspecified number of anti-ship missiles. Damage and fires were reported in at least five Kyiv districts (Darnytskyi, Holosiivskyi, Podilskyi, Shevchenkivskyi, Solomianskyi) plus the outlying Boryspil and Fastiv districts, with at least 16 locations of civilian infrastructure damage citywide. Reported casualties varied by outlet: Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko's office and Al Jazeera cited 5 killed and 30 injured in the capital, while other tallies put it at 3 killed and 19 injured as of the morning of September 8, reflecting the toll's early and evolving state. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said 'his ballistic missiles speak louder than his words on diplomacy,' referring to Vladimir Putin.

title: Russian Drone Hits 'We Are Ukraine' TV Newsroom Live On Air, Injuring Six
detail: As part of the September 8 mass barrage, a Russian Shahed-type attack drone struck the Kyiv building housing the 'We Are Ukraine' and 'We Are Ukraine+' (My-Ukraina) TV channels at midday while the team was broadcasting the national United News telethon live. Six people were injured, three of whom were hospitalized; the strike badly damaged the newsroom and working offices. It was the second strike on the building in weeks — damage from an August 20 attack was still being repaired. President Zelensky condemned the attack and called for an international response, writing on Telegram that 'Shaheds against media is a new page of Russian degradation, and there must certainly be a reaction from Europe and the world.' CPJ and the National Union of Journalists of Ukraine (NUJU) also condemned the strike, with CPJ's Fiona O'Brien noting 'a newsroom is a civilian facility, and journalists are civilians under international law.'

media.caption: Damage at the 'We Are Ukraine' TV newsroom in Kyiv after a Russian drone strike during a live broadcast, Sept. 8, 2026

title: Ukrainian Drone Strikes Kill 4 Across Crimea, Bryansk, Belgorod and Saratov Regions
detail: Overnight Ukrainian drone strikes on September 8 killed at least 4 people and injured 18 across Russian-occupied Crimea and three Russian regions: 2 killed near Simferopol in Crimea, 1 killed and 3 wounded at a gas station in Starodub, Bryansk Oblast, 1 killed and 4 injured across Belgorod Oblast, and 10 injured (including 3 children) in residential areas of Saratov Oblast, where strikes also hit a Rosneft-operated oil refinery. Russia's Defense Ministry said it intercepted 384 Ukrainian drones overnight. The strikes came the same day Russia launched its mass barrage on Kyiv, underscoring that both sides continued mutual attacks after the three-day capitals truce tied to the Witkoff-Kushner diplomatic visit expired.

title: Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Plant's Last External Power Line Restored After 19-Day Outage
detail: Repair crews restored the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant's Ferosplavna-1 external power line on September 8, ending a 19-day outage that had forced the plant to rely on emergency diesel generators to cool its six shut-down reactors and spent fuel pools since the line was severed on August 20 by fighting north of the Dnipro River. The repair was made possible by a seventh IAEA-brokered localized ceasefire, which took effect around September 5-6 to allow demining and technical work near the plant. IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi said the plant's safety systems returned to normal operation, diesel generators were switched to standby, and radiation levels at the site remained normal throughout. Grossi credited both sides for engaging 'constructively with the IAEA to help make this localised ceasefire possible.'
